scored as_is and maximised. A = statutory aggregation (50 full Reg 883/2004 | 30 narrower instrument | 0 none). column1: # route: There is no dataset. Reg 883/2004 and Dir 2014/50 are instruments whose geographic scope the Commission prints as prose - "The rules apply across the EU as well as Iceland Liechtenstein Norway and Switzerland" and "Specific coordination rules also apply to the United Kingdom" - so the figures are read off the law rather than fetched. Transcribed from the Commission's own pages plus EFTA for the EEA incorporation and the Swiss occupational-pension authority for the blocked account.

# coverage: 32 of 32. The whole informational content is two penalties - CH 70 and GB 60 - because 30 rows are identical at 100. reqs.md 6.9 predicted exactly this ("earns its 5% only for the UK"); Switzerland is the second outlier it did not predict

column1: # workings: ASSUMES THE HOUSEHOLD HOLDS EU/EEA/SWISS CITIZENSHIP. The household table is empty so citizenship is unknown; for a third-country national this table is void
column2: because the legal regime is a different one and GB stops being the outlier. Three further caveats. IS/LI/NO component B rests on EFTA's page saying "the Directive on Supplementary Pension Rights" was among 60 acts incorporated on 25 September 2014 - the page does not print the number 2014/50 and that identification is the transcriber's. CH component B is scored at the conservative 10 because no page was found stating Swiss vesting rules meet the Directive's floor even though Swiss law is likely more generous. GB component A rests on the existence of the TCA Protocol on Social Security Coordination rather than on its contents - the Protocol text was never reached in readable form and the DWP guide that looked relevant covers people who moved before 2021.
